[LEXP.8.8.1] **A `const` holds the value the engine computes for its right-hand
side.** The compiler must fold the right-hand side operation by operation, as
the expression associates, to the value the engine computes for the same
expression in a rule ([LDET.3.3a.8]). Each operation's result is that
operation's own. With $\circ(\cdot)$ the binary64 nearest a real value, ties to
even ([LDET.3.6.1]), a `Float` `+` of $a$ and $b$ folds to $\circ(a + b)$, and
the next operation takes that result as its operand. An `Int` result wraps
([LEXP.7.13.1]), and an `Int` operand of a `Float` operation converts first
([LEXP.7.3]).

The compiler must not carry a `Float` subexpression unrounded and round the whole
expression once: the result is a value the engine does not compute. A
transcendental operation folds to [LEXP.3.9.2]'s value, and the compiler computes
every folded operation as [LDET.3.3a.7] requires. An infinity is a value
([LEXP.4.2]), and folds.

The compiler must convert an `Int` result under a `: Float` annotation
([LGRA.4.1]) to the `Float` it promotes to ([LEXP.7.3]). The `const` holds that
`Float`, and a read of it, in a rule or in another `const`, must read that
`Float`.
